g.text: A check from another source: cars seen along Terrebonne on a 2015 night

text.style: font-size: 10px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: Per dwelling addressed on rue de Terrebonne (City roll). Grey: cars counted by eye on the City's 2015 night LiDAR, at the curbs and on the

text.style: font-size: 10px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: lots along the street. Blue: the model's 2024 automobiles per household for the areas holding those dwellings.

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: The two are not the same quantity: the LiDAR sees visitors' cars and the lots of churches, schools and corner buildings, and misses cars inside garages or away;

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: nine years separate them. The check is on the order of magnitude.

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: Sources: SAAQ, vehicles released under the access Act (file 03.06.34729), December 31, 2024, type inferred; Statistics Canada, 2021 Census;

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue'; fill: #5f6b74

g.text: City of Montréal, géobase, parking-sign inventory and assessment roll (CC BY 4.0). Automobiles below the FSA are MODELLED, not measured.
